candidates.title: PAR-A initial per-hydro AR estimation runs single-threaded while the byte-identical classical path already parallelizes the same per-hydro shape

evidence.command: git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/fitting/estimation.rs | sed -n '395,427p'; echo ---; git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/fitting/estimation.rs | sed -n '946,954p'
evidence.reading: estimate_all_hydro_ar_coefficients (classical PACF path) fits every hydro under hydro_ids.par_iter().flat_map_iter(...).collect(); estimate_ar_with_pacf_annual (the PAR(p)-A path) does the identical per-hydro work — conditional_facp_partitioned + estimate_periodic_ar_annual_coefficients per season, pushed to `estimates` — inside a plain serial `for &hydro_id in hydro_ids`. Each annual iteration reads only immutable lookups (group_obs, annual_group_obs, stats_map, annual_stats_map, group_z_year_starts, annual_group_year_starts) and touches only its own hydro's seasons, so it is embarrassingly parallel in exactly the shape the classical site already exploits.

candidates.mechanism: Suspected cost: the PAR-A initial fit is O(n_hydros) independent per-hydro solves (each is n_seasons partitioned-covariance FACP builds + one extended-Yule-Walker Gaussian solve) executed on a single core, whereas the classical fit divides the same n_hydros solves across the rayon pool. As hydro count grows the annual-model fit's wall time stays proportional to n_hydros x per-hydro-solve on one thread while the classical fit is roughly that over the thread count. Deck-independent: the asymmetry is structural (one call parallel, its sibling serial), not tied to any particular deck size. Symbol to profile: estimate_ar_with_pacf_annual (compare against estimate_all_hydro_ar_coefficients on the same hydro set with use_annual_component toggled).
candidates.fixShape: Lift the initial per-hydro block of estimate_ar_with_pacf_annual (the `for &hydro_id in hydro_ids { ... estimates.push(...) }` region) into the same hydro_ids.par_iter().flat_map_iter(|&hydro_id| { build this hydro's Vec<ArCoefficientEstimate> }).collect() shape the classical estimate_all_hydro_ar_coefficients already uses, so each hydro's seasons are produced in its closure and collect reassembles them. The in-code determinism rationale MUST be preserved byte-for-byte: the classical site states 'flat_map_iter/collect reassembles the per-hydro blocks in canonical hydro_ids order, and the inner per-season PACF -> Yule-Walker solve is bit-identical to a single-threaded pass -- thread scheduling cannot change the output. flat_map_iter (not flat_map): each hydro's Vec is small (n_seasons), so nesting work-stealing over it would gain nothing.' The annual closure has the identical property (immutable shared lookups, per-hydro-disjoint output), so canonical-order collect yields the estimates vector in exactly the order the current serial push produces -- apply_annual_prepass_reductions (which rebuilds hydro_indices by EntityId) and build_estimation_report (which sorts by hydro/season) are order-agnostic downstream. Leave the subsequent reduction serial in this change (it mutates `estimates` across hydro index sets). No SDDP paradigm noun, no engine dependency, no new abstraction is introduced.

candidates.title: Per-season correlation matrices recompute every hydro-pair date-set intersection twice and clone the full residual map per (hydro, season)

evidence.command: git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/fitting/correlation.rs | sed -n '396,427p'; echo ---; git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/fitting/correlation.rs | sed -n '447,465p'
evidence.reading: compute_seasonal_matrices, per season, (a) clones every hydro's date-keyed residual map into season_residuals via `.cloned()`, (b) computes min_pairs by walking all O(n_hydros^2) pairs and intersecting the two date sets with contains_key hashes, then (c) if kept, calls compute_pearson_correlation_matrix which walks the SAME O(n_hydros^2) pairs and re-intersects the same date sets via r_j.get(&date). Residuals are produced by compute_hydro_residuals as nested HashMap<usize, HashMap<NaiveDate,f64>>, so each intersection re-hashes every NaiveDate rather than merge-walking a sorted list.

candidates.mechanism: Suspected cost: two multiplied redundancies in the fitting-time correlation build. (1) The per-hydro-pair date-set overlap is computed twice for every kept season -- once as min_pairs, once inside compute_pearson_correlation_matrix -- so the O(n_hydros^2 x observations) intersection work is doubled. (2) Residuals live in HashMap<NaiveDate,f64>, so each of the O(n_hydros^2) pairwise intersections pays a NaiveDate hash per element instead of a linear merge of two date-sorted arrays; compute_pearson_correlation_matrix already sorts the intersected pairs by date afterward, so the hashed layout adds both the hashing and that per-pair sort. (3) `.cloned()` allocates n_hydros x n_seasons fresh HashMaps purely to reshape per-hydro-then-season into per-season-then-hydro. Deck-independent: scales with hydro count squared and residual-series length regardless of deck values. Symbols to profile: compute_seasonal_matrices and compute_pearson_correlation_matrix.
candidates.fixShape: Two independent, fitting-local reductions with no cross-crate blast radius. (i) Compute each pair's overlap count once: have compute_pearson_correlation_matrix (or a shared helper it calls) return the min pair count alongside the matrix, and drop compute_seasonal_matrices' separate min_pairs pre-walk -- or gate the season on the count the matrix build already derives. (ii) Store per-(hydro, season) residuals as a date-sorted Vec<(NaiveDate, f64)> (or one flat sorted buffer) instead of HashMap<NaiveDate,f64>, so the pairwise intersection is a linear merge-walk of two sorted date lists rather than n contains_key/get hashes; this also removes compute_pearson_correlation_matrix's per-pair sort_unstable since the inputs arrive sorted, and lets compute_seasonal_matrices borrow rather than `.cloned()` each hydro's season map. Both the parallel producer and the matrix accumulator carry determinism contracts the fix MUST preserve: compute_hydro_residuals states 'collect() reassembles per-hydro maps in canonical hydro_ids order, and the sequential ar_sum lag accumulation is bit-identical to a single-threaded pass', and compute_pearson_correlation_matrix states 'pairs are summed in NaiveDate order, making every partial sum independent of both HashMap traversal order and which series is row vs column -- so the result is invariant to the declaration order of the input series.' A date-sorted-Vec residual layout upholds both (NaiveDate is a total order within a series; accumulation stays date-ordered).

candidates.title: Per-hydro observation vectors are deep-copied out of group_obs on every estimate/reduce pass (2x classical, 4x PAR-A) though the consumers only read them

evidence.reading: group_obs is a HashMap<(EntityId,usize),Vec<f64>> already owning each hydro-season's observation vector. Every consumer -- the parallel estimate_all_hydro_ar_coefficients closure, the serial reduce_entity_orders, and in the PAR-A path estimate_ar_with_pacf_annual plus reduce_entity_orders_annual -- rebuilds a local obs_by_season: Vec<Vec<f64>> via clone_from(obs), a full deep copy. The reduction and annual-estimate consumers then only read obs (through obs_refs: Vec<&[f64]>).

candidates.mechanism: Suspected cost: the raw observation history is deep-copied out of group_obs (and annual_group_obs) once per pass per hydro -- twice for the classical fit (estimate then reduce) and up to four times for the PAR-A fit (estimate + reduce, each for both Z and A series). Total observation bytes copied is 2x-4x the raw history per fit, all of it discarded after building a Vec<&[f64]> view the solve actually consumes. Deck-independent: copy volume scales with history length x hydro count regardless of deck values. Setup-time (one fit per solve), so it is memory-traffic debt rather than a per-iteration hot path. Symbol to profile: reduce_entity_orders / reduce_entity_orders_annual (allocation volume).
candidates.fixShape: Where the consumer only reads observations (the two reduction loops and the PAR-A initial estimate all build obs_refs: Vec<&[f64]> and pass borrows into the FACP/YW primitives), construct that borrow view directly from group_obs -- e.g. (0..n_seasons).map(|s| group_obs.get(&(hydro_id, s)).map_or(&[][..], Vec::as_slice)).collect() -- instead of clone_from into an owned Vec<Vec<f64>>. group_obs outlives every pass within the fitter, so the borrows are valid. This keeps the classical parallel closure's canonical-order determinism unchanged (it still returns per-hydro results in hydro_ids order) and does not alter any numeric result; it only removes the intermediate owned copies. No paradigm noun, engine dependency, or new abstraction.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/evaluate.rs (evaluate_par_batch, solve_par_noise_batch)
positives.why: The runtime-hot PAR evaluation path is allocation-free: both batch functions write into a caller-supplied &mut [f64] output with debug_assert length checks and no per-call Vec/HashMap, reading psi via PrecomputedPar::psi_slice into the stage-major flat buffer. Nothing to optimize here.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/precompute.rs (PrecomputedPar) and par/lag_kernel.rs (advance_lag_chain, LagIndex)
positives.why: PrecomputedPar is built once at setup into flat Box<[f64]> arrays with a documented stage-major, series-minor, lag-innermost layout keeping a scenario trajectory's per-stage data contiguous for the forward/backward passes; advance_lag_chain is allocation-free, static-dispatched over the LagIndex trait (no Box<dyn>), and operates entirely on caller buffers. Both are cache-conscious and hot-path-clean.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/fitting/{yw_matrices.rs,periodic_ar.rs,partitioned_covariance.rs}
positives.why: The Yule-Walker / FACP primitives are already allocation-conscious: build_periodic_yw_matrix_into writes into caller buffers reused across the increasing-order solves of estimate_periodic_ar_coefficients (matrix_buf/rhs_buf), and conditional_facp_partitioned reuses matrix_buf/rhs_col across its per-lag solves, each with an in-code rationale. solve_linear_system is sized for the small (n<=10) YW systems where the O(n^3) cost is negligible. No per-lag allocation debt to raise.
